tests.title: go.mod declares the module path and Go 1.22 with no require entries
given: the repository root
tests.when: go.mod is read and `go list -m` is run
tests.pseudocode: assert 'module github.com/agent-fox-dev/forked-repo' in go.mod; assert 'go 1.22' in go.mod; assert 'require' not in go.mod

tests.title: cmd/ and internal/ hold empty .gitkeep files and no other top-level directory is added
given: the repository root
tests.when: the tree and git ls-files are inspected
then: cmd/.gitkeep and internal/.gitkeep exist, are empty and are tracked
top-level directories are only cmd, internal, docs (plus .git, .specs)
LICENSE is unchanged versus git HEAD
tests.pseudocode: assert size('cmd/.gitkeep')==0; assert size('internal/.gitkeep')==0; assert git diff --quiet LICENSE

tests.title: git check-ignore reports none of the required paths as ignored
given: the repository .gitignore
tests.when: git check-ignore is run for cmd/.gitkeep, internal/.gitkeep, Makefile, docs/generated/.gitkeep and docs/generated/root.txt
tests.pseudocode: for p in paths: assert run('git check-ignore -q', p).status == 1

tests.title: bin/ is ignored by git
given: the repository .gitignore
tests.pseudocode: assert run('git check-ignore bin/x').status == 0

tests.title: All eight targets are declared .PHONY and help is the default goal
given: the Makefile
tests.when: `make -p -n` output and the .PHONY line are inspected
then: help, build, test, fmt, vet, check, doc, clean are all in .PHONY
tests.pseudocode: assert set(targets) <= phony_targets; assert default_goal == 'help'

tests.title: make and make help list every target with a description
given: the skeleton
then: output has a line for each of help, build, test, fmt, vet, check, doc, clean
tests.pseudocode: for cmd in ['make','make help']: r=run(cmd); assert r.status==0; for t in targets: assert line_with(t, r.out)

tests.title: make build/test/vet exit status mirrors the underlying go command and build writes binaries to bin/
given: a temp copy of the skeleton with a main package under cmd/app
then a copy with a compile error in that package
tests.when: make build, make test and make vet are run in each copy
then: in the valid copy all exit 0 and bin/app exists after build
in the broken copy make build exits non-zero like go build
tests.pseudocode: assert make('build').status == 0; assert exists('bin/app'); break(); assert make('build').status != 0

tests.title: make fmt rewrites an unformatted Go file
given: a temp copy with an unformatted valid .go file
tests.pseudocode: assert make('fmt').status==0; assert run('gofmt -l .').out==''

tests.title: make check runs fmt, vet, build, test in order and exits 0 on success
given: the skeleton
then: the commands appear in order fmt, vet, build, test (via make -n)
tests.pseudocode: order = make('-n check'); assert idx(fmt)<idx(vet)<idx(build)<idx(test); assert make('check').status==0

tests.title: A failing vet step stops make check before build and test
given: a temp copy with a Go file that go vet rejects (e.g. Printf format mismatch)
then: no output from the go build or go test steps, and bin/ not created
tests.pseudocode: r=make('check'); assert r.status!=0; assert 'ok' not in r.out; assert not exists('bin')

tests.title: make clean removes only bin/ and succeeds when it is absent
given: a temp copy with bin/x, docs/generated/.gitkeep and cmd/.gitkeep
tests.pseudocode: assert make('clean').status==0; assert not exists('bin'); assert make('clean').status==0; assert snapshot_minus_bin == before

tests.title: All go-based targets exit 0 on the empty tree and gofmt -l is silent
given: the skeleton with no .go files
tests.when: make build, test, vet, fmt, check and doc are each run, then gofmt -l .
tests.pseudocode: for t in [...]: assert make(t).status==0; assert run('gofmt -l .').out==''

tests.title: make doc on the empty tree leaves docs/generated/ with only .gitkeep
given: the skeleton with docs/generated/ absent
tests.pseudocode: make('doc'); assert listdir('docs/generated')==['.gitkeep']

tests.title: make doc writes one file per public package and skips internal and examples packages
given: a temp module with packages root, util, internal/x, a/internal, examples/e and a/examples
then: files exist only for the root and util packages
tests.pseudocode: assert make('doc').status==0; assert sorted(listdir)==['.gitkeep','root.txt','util.txt']; assert content(util.txt)==go_doc_all(util)

tests.title: Output file name is the module-relative import path with / replaced by _ plus .txt
given: a temp module with generated public package trees
tests.when: for any public package path of one or more non-internal, non-examples segments (or the module root)
then: its doc file is named segments joined by _ plus .txt, or root.txt for the root
tests.pseudocode: for pkg in gen_pkgs(): make('doc'); assert exists('docs/generated/' + ('root' if pkg=='' else pkg.replace('/','_')) + '.txt')

tests.title: Stale generated files are deleted on regeneration
given: a temp module where make doc has generated util.txt, then package util is removed and a stale old.txt is added
tests.pseudocode: rm('util'); make('doc'); assert listdir=='.gitkeep' only

tests.title: make doc exits non-zero when go doc fails for a public package
given: a temp module with a public package and GO set to a wrapper that fails on `doc` but delegates otherwise
tests.pseudocode: r=make('doc GO=./failing_go'); assert r.status != 0

tests.title: The Makefile uses no GNU-only or bash-only constructs and runs under make 3.81 and GNU make
given: the Makefile
tests.when: it is scanned for .ONESHELL, $(file, grouped targets (&:), [[ ]], process substitution, arrays, and run under GNU make and (if available) make 3.81 with `make help` and `make check`
then: recipes invoke only go and POSIX tools
tests.pseudocode: assert not regex('\\.ONESHELL|\\$\\(file|&:|\\[\\[|<\\(', Makefile); assert make('help').status==0

tests.title: Every go invocation uses the GO variable with default go
given: a recording wrapper script as GO
tests.when: make check and make doc are run with GO=<wrapper> and then with the variable passed via environment
then: every recorded go call came from the wrapper
tests.pseudocode: make('check doc GO=wrapper'); assert log nonempty; assert no direct 'go ' call outside wrapper

tests.title: The four docs files exist with their required statements
given: the repository root
tests.when: docs/architecture.md, api.md, cli.md and configuration.md are read
then: architecture.md mentions cmd/, internal/, docs/generated/ and the module path
api.md states no REST or public Go API yet
cli.md states no CLI yet and names all eight make targets
configuration.md states no config keys apart from the GO variable
tests.pseudocode: assert contains(architecture, module_path); assert contains(cli, each target)

tests.title: README keeps its title and description and gains layout, Go version and targets
given: README.md
then: it still starts with `# upstream-repo` and the original description line
it mentions cmd/, internal/, Go 1.22 and the make targets
tests.pseudocode: assert lines[0]=='# upstream-repo'; assert '1.22' in readme

tests.title: A fresh checkout passes make check with only the Go toolchain
given: a clean clone of the repository with only Go and POSIX tools on PATH
then: no files are created outside the tree
git status shows no untracked build output
tests.pseudocode: clone(); assert make('check').status==0; assert git_status_clean_or_only_expected

tests.title: make doc regenerates docs/generated/ end to end
given: a clone with a stale docs/generated/old.txt and a public package added
then: the package's .txt exists with go doc -all output
tests.pseudocode: touch old.txt; make('doc'); assert not exists(old.txt); assert exists('docs/generated/pkg.txt')

tests.title: A developer builds, sees bin/ ignored and cleans
given: a clone with a main package under cmd/app
tests.when: make build, git status, then make clean (twice) are run
then: git status lists nothing under bin/
clean exits 0 and removes bin/, also when bin/ is absent
tests.pseudocode: make('build'); assert 'bin/' not in git_status(); make('clean'); assert make('clean').status==0
